To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a new drug, which is composed of des-acetyl-vinblastin covalently linked through an enzymatically cleavable peptide bond to a peptide containing a sequence recognized by prostate-specific antigen, has been synthesized and shown to be selectively toxic to cells in vitro and animals in vivo that express prostate-specific antigen.
a new drug that is composed of vinblastine linked to a peptide bond that is hydrolyzed by PSA is highly effective and well tolerated in animals bearing prostate tumors.
a PSA hydrolyzable vinca alkaloid conjugate selectively killed PSA-secreting tumor cells and was minimally toxic in vivo in animals and in dogs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new class of anticancer agents, the PSA-activated prodrugs, for the treatment of patients with androgen-refractory prostate cancer.
the design of a new class of chemotherapeutic agents for prostate cancer.
the design and evaluation of a PSA-activated vinblastine-congenate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the vinblastine pro-drug is a promising new agent for treating men with advanced prostate cancer.
this new drug has been shown to selectively kill prostate cancer cells and to do so without significant toxicity to the host.
this new chemotherapeutic agent is a promising experimental drug candidate for the treatment of men with advanced prostate cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed and characterized an experimental prostate cancer therapy which is minimally toxic in dogs and which shows excellent antitumor activity in mice.
a PSA-activated vinblastine-congener is a promising experimental therapy for prostate carcinoma.
the vinblastine conjugate is a novel, selective, and highly potent chemotherapeutic agent for the treatment of prostate cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the vinblastine-peptide conjugate is a promising new agent for the treatment of prostate cancer.
we have developed a new class of drugs that are activated by a tumor-specific enzyme.
the PSA-activated prodrug concept has been validated in a preclinical setting.
